answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, non-transferable work bond: a new agent must complete verifiable tasks attested by established peers before it can trade. Like a pearl formed layer by layer, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. A mirror check compares behaviour across identities, so clones acting in lockstep on the same ridge of tasks stand out. Creating thousands of fakes then costs thousands of bonds and months of work, while one honest agent pays once.
